messages:
sam: Quick brain-dump — I'm sketching a refactor for segmented rollouts where the routing decision uses a lightweight dependency graph to pick origins and a separate fast-path degrade when origin latency spikes. Thoughts?
rachel: Love the separation idea. Do you mean the graph lives in control-plane and is pushed to edge routers? Or computed per-request?
sam: Control-plane pushes a compact DAG per-route. Routers evaluate locally. Graph nodes = origin variants + predicate edges (pct, geo, capacity). Keeps runtime cheap.
ev an: How do we do fast fallback? timers? circuit-breaker?
sam: Two-tier: (1) soft bypass: if origin RSV > threshold for N reqs -> reroute to backup origin in graph within 50ms; (2) hard degrade: fallback to hosted smaller model or cached response after hard ttl_ms window. Both decisions local to router.
kai: Need to be careful with statefulness — per-client session affinity + graph updates can conflict.
rachel: Agree; propose leases for graph versions and an epoch in the routing header. Routers reject older epoch changes until they finish draining.
sam: Sketch of policy blob:
```
rollout_graph_v: 12
nodes:
  - id: v2
    pct: 10
    origins: ["v2-a","v2-b"]
edges:
  - from: root
    to: v2
    when: "pct:10 && region:eu"
fallback:
  soft_threshold_ms: 200
  soft_fail_count: 3
  hard_ttl_ms: 5000
```
ev an: +1 for numeric thresholds. Also add token-slice awareness to avoid cross-tenant amplification.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: push/graph:v12 -> edge-nodes (12/48) started @ 2026-03-20T15:02Z
ops-oncall: What about telemetry? we need per-origin P99 latency + drop-rate and a synthetic canary probe.
kai: Also consider degenerate case: graph edge config changes while sessions mid-flight -> attach origin lineage to each session so replies stay consistent.
rachel: Interface boundary idea — make graph evaluation API pure function: input (route_headers, session_state, rnd) => origin_set, and a separate actuator that enforces TTL/circuit decisions. Keeps testability.
sam: Final q: do we make graph expressive (predicates, JS) or keep a small DSL? I'm leaning small DSL for verification.
ev an: small DSL + opt-in predicate extension via sandboxed wasm if really needed.
sam: Cool. I'll iterate on RFC with these points. thanks! :thumbsup:
